target.title: fix(agents): keep subagent run ID mask from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the subagent run-ID mask used in lifecycle log/error metadata could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the run ID contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`maskRunId` sliced its prefix/suffix with raw `String.prototype.slice`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the masked ID always falls on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The helper lives at module scope; after the hardened deadcode gate flagged the test-only export, coverage now exercises it through the lifecycle controller's public warning surface instead of a direct import.

## User Impact

Subagent lifecycle warnings and error metadata remain well-formed when run IDs contain non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Moved `maskRunId` to module scope in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` and exported it.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` covering ASCII masking and astral boundary cases.
- Existing lifecycle controller tests continue to pass.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a run ID like `"abc😀xxxxxxxxx"` produced `"abc\ud83d…\ude00xxxx"` (isolated surrogate halves). After the patch it returns `"abc…xxxx"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/mask-runid-utf16` at `71f75fbfa526d0041851c3530662325cc35ac424`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; for (const v of ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b", "short"]) console.log(JSON.stringify(maskRunId(v)));'
  ```
  And to verify the masked values survive a real disk round-trip without corrupting:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "mr-")), "m.txt"); const samples = ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b"]; const masked = samples.map(maskRunId); writeFileSync(f, masked.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === masked.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  "run-…7890"
  "abc…xxxx"
  "xxxx…abc"
  "***"

  run-…7890
  abc…xxxx
  xxxx…abc
  ***
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at mask boundaries` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every masked value, no isolated surrogates are emitted, and the joined masked values survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live subagent lifecycle failure path; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

_AI-assisted PR: changes and tests were generated with AI assistance and manually reviewed._



## Follow-up: merge with current main + deadcode policy fix

Merged `upstream/main` (test-file conflict resolved by keeping both the upstream settle-wake block and this mask coverage). Dropped the unnecessary `export` on `maskRunId` to satisfy the hard-zero Knip policy and converted the focused unit test into behavior assertions on `runId` masking in lifecycle finalization warnings (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` — 106/106 pass). Exact head: `b3ec348b83fe00477a051b0a3db57825331a7549` (follow-up commit avoids String(unknown) in the warning capture to satisfy oxlint typescript/no-base-to-string in CI check-lint; test-only, 106/106 still pass).

target.title: fix(diagnostics): prevent memory growth from completed session churn
target.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
For fixes, begin with:
"Fixes an issue where users <do X> would <experience Y> when <condition>."
or:
"Resolves a problem where..."

Name the affected UI surface or workflow. Do not describe the code-level cause here.
-->

Fixes an issue where long-running Gateway processes retained diagnostic references for every completed session, allowing process-local memory use to grow continuously under session churn.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
In one or two sentences, explain the complete shipped solution, key design
decisions, and relevant boundaries or non-goals. Include implementation detail
only when it helps reviewers understand user-visible behavior or risk.
Avoid file-by-file narration.
-->

Diagnostic run activity now separates session aliases from sequenced active-run ownership, retains completion guards while matching asynchronous events are still queued, and prunes only idle activity with a 30-minute retention and 2,000-entry ceiling. Stuck-session recovery retires only recovered owners while preserving newer work, and run-less reply operations hold explicit activity ownership until their registry lifecycle ends. No public API, configuration, or protocol changes are introduced.

## User Impact

<!--
State what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect. Lead with the
concrete benefit and use user-facing language. If there is no user-visible
impact, say so plainly.
-->

Operators can keep Gateway processes running through high session churn without completed diagnostic activity growing without bound, while current activity remains available to staleness and recovery diagnostics.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. Include before/after evidence for visual
changes when it clarifies the result.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
-->

- Exact-head build: `pnpm build` passed at `7267377e358` in 8m 50s, including the production bundles, UI build, and post-build checks.
- Exact-head live Gateway: an isolated built Gateway processed 2,500 completed-session lifecycles through the production diagnostic event path. Retained completed activity plateaued at 1,997 entries; the oldest completed session was evicted and the newest remained.
- Lifecycle guards in the same live run: a queued late progress event did not reactivate its completed run; stuck-session recovery retired the recovered owner while preserving newer work; an active run-less reply operation and a separate active run both survived churn.
- Identifier-free tool lifecycle regression: 2,001 paired start/completion events without run or session identifiers did not consume retained session activity; the focused run-activity suite passed 9/9 tests.
- Availability check: `diagnostics.stability` succeeded over Gateway RPC after churn and returned the expected stability payload fields.
- Regression coverage on the submitted tree includes bounded completed-session churn, queued-event completion guards, recovered-owner retirement, and run-less reply-operation retention through completion.

target.title: fix(agents): bound GitHub release JSON response body in tools-manager
target.body:
## Summary
Replace unbounded `response.json()` in `getLatestVersion` with `readProviderJsonResponse()` so GitHub release-check responses are read under a byte cap.

## What Problem This Solves
The tool binary manager (`ensureTool`) fetches the latest release tag from `https://api.github.com/repos/<repo>/releases/latest` to resolve download URLs. The success path calls `response.json()` directly, which buffers the entire response body into memory without any size limit.

If the GitHub API endpoint is compromised, misconfigured, or replaced by a proxy that returns an oversized payload, the runtime would buffer an unbounded body before parsing — potentially exhausting memory.

**Code evidence**: In `src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts:164`, the current code:
```typescript
const data = (await response.json()) as { tag_name: string };
```
reads the entire response body with no byte cap.

This is the same pattern fixed across the codebase (e.g., `readProviderJsonResponse` in provider HTTP utilities, `readResponseWithLimit` in fetch guards) but was missed here because `getLatestVersion` is a small internal helper rather than a primary provider adapter.

## Root Cause
- The `fetchWithSsrFGuard` wrapper provides a connection/signal timeout, but the response body read via `response.json()` is not bounded.
- Other call sites in `src/agents/` use `readProviderJsonResponse()` (which caps at 16 MiB by default), but `tools-manager.ts` used the raw `response.json()` API directly.
- The existing `readProviderJsonResponse` helper was already available in `src/agents/provider-http-errors.ts` but was not imported here.

## Why This Fix
- **Chosen approach**: Replace `response.json()` with `readProviderJsonResponse<{ tag_name: string }>(response, "tools-manager release check")`, reusing the existing bounded reader.
- **Why**: Zero new infrastructure — the bounded reader already handles byte capping, chunk timeouts, and idle timeouts. The default 16 MiB cap is far larger than any legitimate GitHub release JSON payload.
- **Alternatives considered**: Inline `readResponseWithLimit` + `JSON.parse` would duplicate the pattern already abstracted in `readProviderJsonResponse`.

## User Impact
- **Normal path**: GitHub returns a small release JSON → identical behavior, no user-visible change.
- **Degraded path**: An oversized or malicious response is rejected early with a clear error (`tools-manager release check: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`) instead of silently buffering until OOM.
- **Affected operation**: `ensureTool("fd")` / `ensureTool("rg")` → the GitHuber release version probe.

## Evidence
- **Before**: `response.json()` buffers entire body with no size cap — a 100 MiB response from a compromised endpoint would allocate 100 MiB of memory.
- **After**: `readProviderJsonResponse()` caps at 16 MiB and rejects oversized bodies with a descriptive error. The bounded reader also enforces chunk-level idle timeouts so a slow-drip response cannot stall the read indefinitely.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
# In getLatestVersion, the success path calls response.json() directly.
# No byte cap, no idle timeout on the body read — the runtime buffers the
# entire response before parsing, regardless of size.
# Proof: grep -n "response.json()" src/agents/utils/tools-manager.ts
# 164:    const data = (await response.json()) as { tag_name: string };
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
# getLatestVersion now uses readProviderJsonResponse with a 16 MiB default cap:
#   const data = await readProviderJsonResponse<{ tag_name: string }>(
#     response,
#     "tools-manager release check",
#   );
# Runtime behavior:
#   - 200 + small JSON → parses and returns { tag_name } (unchanged)
#   - Oversized body > 16 MiB → throws "tools-manager release check: JSON
#     response exceeds 16777216 bytes" before full buffering
#   - Slow drip (stalled chunk) → aborted by idle timeout
```

## Tests and Validation
- `npx vitest run src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` — 18 tests passed (2 files × 9 tests)
- New regression test: "bounds release-check JSON response body to prevent unbounded buffering" — verifies both the release-check and download fetch guards are released after a successful bounded read
- The existing test "cancels download error bodies before releasing guarded fetches" continues to pass (it exercises the same release-check path with a bounded read on the 200 response)

target.title: fix: gateway boots when a configured plugin payload is broken
target.body:
Refs #109833

PR #110200 has merged into `main`; this branch is rebased onto its merge result.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where gateway readiness would be blocked when a configured and enabled plugin package failed startup verification, even though the failure belonged to a known plugin surface that could be isolated.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the operator decision on #109833: degrade and boot. Startup quarantines the known plugin owner, emits its typed verification diagnostic once, and skips that plugin before any plugin code can load. Doctor, status, and health expose every quarantined plugin as `configured-unavailable`.

The behavior mirrors degraded SecretRef owners in `src/secrets/runtime-degraded-state.ts` and configured-unavailable channels in `src/channels/status/read-model.ts`. It also follows the root `AGENTS.md` security policy that failures isolate to the smallest known owning surface. The explicit `openclaw update` convergence path remains unchanged and continues to report payload convergence failures prominently.

## User Impact

Operators can keep the gateway ready when one configured plugin package is broken, while the broken plugin remains fully unavailable for that boot and its typed reason stays visible in operational diagnostics. State-migration failures, structurally invalid config, and startup failures with unknown ownership still block readiness.

## Summary

- Records enabled-plugin verification failures as boot-stable quarantine state.
- Prevents quarantined plugins from reaching artifact resolution or import.
- Projects the degraded state through doctor, status, and health, with install paths redacted from public diagnostics.
- Leaves disabled-plugin findings non-degraded and preserves unrelated convergence blockers.

## Root Cause

Before this change, `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` converted every plugin convergence warning into a fatal startup diagnostic. The design contract in `src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.ts` explicitly required refusing restart whenever an active installed plugin payload was unloadable, so a known plugin-owned package failure blocked the entire gateway.

PR #110200 supplies the typed package-verification reasons, including unreadable `package.json`. This change replaces the startup-only fail-closed contract with quarantine: the owner is known, so the plugin is not loaded and the rest of the gateway may become ready. Migration and config validation gates are untouched.

## Real behavior proof

Closest feasible isolated gateway scenario:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-startup-plugin-quarantine.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

The scenario creates a configured plugin whose declared entry fails static verification, records the real typed finding, and starts a real gateway server. It observes HTTP 200 with `{ "ready": true }` from `/readyz`, while an import sentinel proves the quarantined plugin's top-level code never ran. Registry and health diagnostics report the plugin unavailable without exposing its install path.

## Evidence

Focused quarantine, preflight, doctor, status, health, and gateway coverage:

```text

  src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.state-migration.test.ts \
  src/commands/status.summary.test.ts \
```

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       54 passed (54)
```

target.title: fix(sessions): estimate file content size before Buffer allocation

## What Problem This Solves

The `sessions.files.set` handler allocated `Buffer.from(params.content, "utf8")` before checking the 256 KiB preview limit. An oversized request therefore materialized its complete encoded payload only to reject it immediately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The handler now obtains the exact UTF-8 byte count with `Buffer.byteLength` first. Only accepted content is encoded into a Buffer for the existing strict round-trip safety check. The protocol schema intentionally stays byte-limit agnostic: a character-count limit would not enforce this UTF-8 byte contract.

Maintainer follow-up tightened the regression test: multibyte input proves byte accounting, and a `Buffer.from` spy proves rejection happens before encoded-buffer allocation.

## User Impact

No behavior or API change. Oversized session-file writes still return `session_file_too_large` with the exact byte size, but avoid the redundant allocation.

Repo architecture rules require typed presentation actions over raw string inference, and the marker was PR1's explicit stopgap (never reachable from a release tag, so not a shipped contract). This PR gives structured questions a real, typed producer path end to end.

target.title: fix(agents): guard JSON.parse against malformed payloadJSON from paired node
target.body:
## Summary
Wrap `JSON.parse(result.payloadJSON)` in try-catch within `parseNodeClaudeResultPayload` and `parseNodeClaudeApprovalRequired` so a malformed payload from a remote paired node does not throw an uncaught `SyntaxError`.

## What Problem This Solves
When `executeNodeClaudeRun` receives a result from a paired node via `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun()`, the `payloadJSON` field is serialized JSON from that remote node. Two internal parse helpers — `parseNodeClaudeResultPayload` and `parseNodeClaudeApprovalRequired` — both call `JSON.parse(result.payloadJSON)` without a try-catch guard.

If the paired node sends malformed JSON (corrupted transit, bug in the node agent, or a misconfigured proxy), the `SyntaxError` thrown by `JSON.parse` propagates uncaught, bypassing the existing "invalid result" error path and potentially crashing the caller.

**Code evidence**: In `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-node-claude.ts`, the parse helpers used:
```typescript
const value = result.payloadJSON ? (JSON.parse(result.payloadJSON) as unknown) : result.payload;
```
— a bare `JSON.parse` on data from a remote source with no catch.

The existing code at lines 251 and 362 already calls these functions within the `executeNodeClaudeRun` flow, so a malformed payload from a real paired node would surface this.

## Root Cause
- `payloadJSON` originates from `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun()` — a remote paired node over the network.
- Both parse helpers assumed `payloadJSON` is always valid JSON without a guard.
- The `parseNodeClaudeResultPayload` function already throws `"paired node returned an invalid Claude CLI result"` for shape mismatches; malformed JSON should produce a similarly descriptive error instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.
- The `parseNodeClaudeApprovalRequired` function returns `null` for invalid shapes; malformed JSON should produce `null` (not a throw) to match the existing "invalid → null" contract.

## Why This Fix
- **parseNodeClaudeResultPayload**: catch → throw `new Error("paired node returned malformed JSON in Claude CLI result")` — consistent with the existing `"invalid Claude CLI result"` error pattern, provides a clear diagnostic.
- **parseNodeClaudeApprovalRequired**: catch → return `null` — consistent with the function's existing contract of returning `null` for any invalid/missing data.
- **Alternative considered**: a shared helper function, but the two functions have different failure contracts (throw vs. return null), so inline try-catch is clearer.

## User Impact
- **Normal path**: Paired node returns valid JSON → identical behavior, no user-visible change.
- **Degraded path**: Malformed payloadJSON from paired node:
  - Before: `SyntaxError` propagates uncaught → caller crashes or gets a confusing error.
  - After: clear error message `"paired node returned malformed JSON in Claude CLI result"` or graceful `null` return, handled by existing error paths.

## Evidence
- **Before**: `JSON.parse(result.payloadJSON)` on malformed input throws uncaught `SyntaxError`, which propagates past the existing shape-validation guards.
- **After**: Malformed JSON is caught and converted to a descriptive error (for `parseNodeClaudeResultPayload`) or a graceful `null` return (for `parseNodeClaudeApprovalRequired`), matching each function's existing error contract.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
# parseNodeClaudeResultPayload({ payloadJSON: "not-valid{{{ " })
# → throws SyntaxError: "Unexpected token '{{{'..." — uncaught, bypasses validation
#
# parseNodeClaudeApprovalRequired({ ok: true, payloadJSON: "<<<bad>>>" })
# → throws SyntaxError — instead of returning null as the contract specifies
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx proof.mjs
# parseNodeClaudeResultPayload({ payloadJSON: "not-valid{{{ " })
# → throws Error: "paired node returned malformed JSON in Claude CLI result"
#
# parseNodeClaudeApprovalRequired({ ok: true, payloadJSON: "<<<bad>>>" })
# → returns null (contract-preserving)
```

target.title: fix(cli): exit cleanly on startup migration refusal
target.body:
## Summary

- report the three planned startup migration/config/plugin refusal reasons at their owner, then throw `ExitError(1)` so `ensureConfigReady` uses its existing typed `runtime.exit` path
- add a hermetic child-process regression that exercises a real conflicting plugin-state migration, requires exit status 1 with no signal, verifies the refusal appears exactly once, and confirms the startup migration lease is released
- audit the core `DatabaseSync` migration/checkpoint paths for throw-time handle leaks; every direct handle is already closed by `finally`, so no unrelated migration refactor is included

This PR was originally stacked on #110200. That prerequisite has now merged as `748fc044192a1c98d8344ea6682a3f38dd7ef384`; the branch was rebased onto `origin/main` at `82fa956d5a22c65d0dd9f2bfc5ff964e45c9728e`, and the already-applied `ce6e200aaa2` commit dropped from this PR's history. The landing dependency is satisfied.

Refs #109831.

## What Problem This Solves

Startup migration, invalid-config, and plugin-verification refusals were ordinary `Error`s. They bypassed the typed exit handling in `src/cli/program/config-guard.ts`, reached the generic `src/entry.ts` failure handler, and ended in its direct `process.exit(1)` path. In the reported supervised deployment, that path terminated with signal 11 / status 139 instead of a clean refusal status, turning a fail-closed migration result into a supervisor crash loop.

## Root Cause

The proven pre-fix control flow is:

1. `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` formatted an intentional readiness refusal but threw a plain `Error`.
2. `ensureConfigReady` only converts `ExitError` into `runtime.exit(error.code)`, so it rethrew the plain refusal.
3. `src/entry.ts` added `Could not start the CLI.` / `Reason:` formatting and called `process.exit(1)`.

The preflight's existing `finally` already releases its heartbeat and startup migration lease before the error leaves the owner. The fix preserves that unwind and hands the intentional refusal to the typed caller contract instead of treating it as an unexpected CLI startup failure.

The reporter's exact native signal source is not established without their core dump. This change fixes the incorrect refusal path and locks down the observable process contract; it does not claim to identify or patch the native module.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal owner must print the reason because the typed `ExitError` branch intentionally does not format errors, while the generic entry catch is no longer reached. Printing once immediately before throwing `ExitError(1)` preserves the complete operator guidance without duplicating the generic wrapper.

This is the narrow owner-boundary fix: unexpected preflight errors still use the generic failure handler, and gateway readiness remains fail-closed.

The core migration audit covered the direct `DatabaseSync` constructors in `src/infra/state-migrations.debug-proxy.ts`, `src/infra/state-migrations.task-sidecar-rows.ts`, and `src/infra/state-migrations.storage.ts`, plus the checkpoint database wrapper used by `src/infra/startup-migration-checkpoint.ts`. Each closes in `finally`, including throw paths. No plugin-owned code was changed.

## User Impact

When a startup migration gate refuses readiness, operators retain the full actionable refusal text exactly once. The CLI exits through the typed status-1 path, the migration lease is released, and supervisors see a normal non-zero exit rather than a signal in the covered regression environment.

## Evidence

### Rebase result

After #110200 merged, `git fetch origin main` and `git rebase origin/main` skipped its already-applied `ce6e200aaa2` commit and replayed only this PR's fix. Main advanced once during the proof window, so the branch was rebased a second time before the final proof.

`git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` on the published branch contains one commit:

```text
d0281e2cc2a fix(cli): exit cleanly on migration refusal
```

Final identities:

```text
origin/main=82fa956d5a22c65d0dd9f2bfc5ff964e45c9728e
head=d0281e2cc2a852f2c20903275fa7fa74ac996c92
```

### Real behavior proof — exact rebased head

Environment: Linux source checkout, Node `v25.9.0`, actual `src/entry.ts`, no provider/channel credentials, and an isolated realpathed temporary `HOME`, config, and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. The canonical plugin-state row had timestamp 2000 and value `{"version":1}`; the legacy sidecar held the same key with newer timestamp 3000 and divergent value `{"version":2}`. That is intentionally unresolved under the merged #109832 migration contract.

A Node supervisor wrapper used `spawnSync` with a 60-second timeout and captured the wait status and signal separately. It launched the actual gateway entry twice against the same unresolved state:

```text
node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway run --allow-unconfigured
```

Observed on exact head `d0281e2cc2a852f2c20903275fa7fa74ac996c92`:

```text
gateway_run_1 status=1 signal=none refusal_count=1 stale_lease_count=0 generic_wrapper_count=0
after_gateway_run_1 active_startup_migration_lease=false
gateway_run_2 status=1 signal=none refusal_count=1 stale_lease_count=0 generic_wrapper_count=0
after_gateway_run_2 active_startup_migration_lease=false
```

Redacted stderr from the first run:

```text
[state-migrations] Legacy state migration warnings:
- Left plugin-state sidecar in place because 1 row differs from shared state without a newer canonical timestamp. First key: proof-plugin/proof-namespace/proof-key
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Left plugin-state sidecar in place because 1 row differs from shared state without a newer canonical timestamp. First key: proof-plugin/proof-namespace/proof-key
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
```

This proves both supervisor-observed gateway attempts exited with code 1 rather than a signal/status 139, printed the refusal headline exactly once on stderr, omitted the generic outer-entry wrapper, and released the startup migration lease. The second run acquired a fresh lease and did not report a stale/active lease.

### Doctor-path parity

The same exact-head wrapper and unresolved fixture then ran:

```text
node --import tsx src/entry.ts doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes
```

Observed:

```text
doctor_fix status=0 signal=none stale_lease_count=0 active_startup_migration_lease=false
```

Doctor continues to report the unresolved migration without gating gateway readiness, exits normally, and releases its lease. Gateway remains fail-closed on the next startup attempt.

### Guard-boundary verification

The existing `ensureConfigReady` catch in `src/cli/program/config-guard.ts` intercepts `ExitError` and calls `runtime.exit(error.code)`. The live process transcript proves the refusal reaches that branch: the generic `[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.` wrapper count is zero, while the refusal owner prints its reason exactly once.

### Post-rebase fixture correction

The first focused run after rebasing failed because merged #109832 correctly archived the old fixture's older sidecar row; the child then continued to a locally occupied gateway port. That was a stale test premise, not a product regression. The fixture now uses a newer divergent sidecar timestamp, which is the migration state that must remain unresolved. The corrected exact-head run is green.

Mandatory uncommitted autoreview of that fixture correction reported:

```text
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.98)
```

### Pre-fix contrast and native-crash boundary

An earlier run from pre-fix merge base `433b3ce86d71a88fb34d4f61f6f10c36b912aeee` exited status 1 with no signal on this host, but included `generic_wrapper_count=1`; the patched path has `generic_wrapper_count=0`. The reporter's SIGSEGV did not reproduce in this environment on either revision. This proof establishes the clean typed-exit contract owned by this PR; identifying the reporter's crashing native module remains deferred pending their core dump.

### Verification

```text
pnpm format src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts
Finished in 4ms on 1 files using 1 threads.

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.state-migration.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.process.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       24 passed (24)
Duration    2.51s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 4.62s

git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
passed
```

## What Was Not Tested

- The reporter's exact container/supervisor/native-module failure was not reproduced; identifying the crashing native module requires the reporter's core dump and is intentionally deferred.
- No successful full gateway channel/provider startup was exercised. The real child process stops at the intended preflight refusal, before `runGatewayCommand` starts runtime services.
- No broad suite was run; focused coverage exercises the changed refusal owner, existing migration cases, child-process exit semantics, lease cleanup, and the scoped core changed gate.

target.title: fix(tailscale): guard parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject against malformed output
target.body:
## Summary
Guard `parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject` against malformed tailscale CLI output so that non-JSON stdout returns an empty object instead of throwing.

## What Problem This Solves
The `parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject()` function in `src/infra/tailscale.ts` is named to acknowledge that tailscale CLI output may contain noise (log lines, warnings) mixed with JSON. The function extracts the JSON portion and calls `JSON.parse()`, but the parse calls were unwrapped — no try-catch. If the output is entirely non-JSON (e.g., a daemon connection error message), the function throws an uncaught exception that propagates to callers.

**Code evidence**: In `src/infra/tailscale.ts:21-23`, two `JSON.parse()` calls have no try-catch guard despite the function name promising tolerance of noisy input.

## Root Cause
- The function's contract says "possibly noisy" but doesn't handle the case where the noise overwhelms the JSON
- Trigger: tailscale daemon is not running or produces error output → stdout contains a plain-text error message → `JSON.parse` throws

## Why This Fix
Wrap both `JSON.parse` calls in a single try-catch, returning `{}` on parse failure. This is consistent with how the callers already treat the result (they check for specific keys and fall back gracefully). Returning empty object preserves the existing caller behavior — all callers use `parsed.Self?.DNSName` / `parsed.Self?.TailscaleIPs` with optional chaining, so a missing key is handled.

## User Impact
Tailscale-dependent features (tailnet hostname discovery, funnel status checks, whois lookups) now degrade gracefully when the tailscale CLI produces unexpected output, instead of throwing an uncaught exception.

## Evidence
- `npx vitest run src/infra/tailscale.test.ts` — 6 passed (empty input, non-JSON text, truncated JSON, command error messages, valid JSON, noisy JSON)
- `git diff --check` clean

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main)
```bash
$ node --import tsx -e "
const { parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject } = require('./src/infra/tailscale.ts');
parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject('connection refused');
"
# throws: SyntaxError: Unexpected token c in JSON at position 0
```

### After (with fix)
```bash
$ node --import tsx -e "
const { parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject } = require('./src/infra/tailscale.ts');
console.log(parsePossiblyNoisyJsonObject('connection refused'));
"
# {}
```

## Tests and Validation
- `npx vitest run src/infra/tailscale.test.ts` passed (6/6)
- `git diff --check` clean

target.title: fix(agents): honor abort signal during compaction summary retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`summarizeChunks` in `src/agents/compaction.ts` retries summary generation via `retryAsync`. The mandatory `params.signal` is already forwarded to `generateSummary` and checked in `shouldRetry`, but the backoff sleep between attempts used the default unabortable timer. When a user cancels a session mid-compaction, the retry loop still waits out the full backoff (500ms–5s with jitter) before the abort is noticed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`retryAsync` accepts a custom `sleep`; this passes `sleepWithAbort(ms, params.signal)` (imported from `../infra/backoff.js`, the same source as `src/agents/api-key-rotation.ts`). An abort during the backoff now rejects the sleep, which propagates through `retryAsync` unwrapped — the existing `signal.aborted` checks in `summarizeChunks`/`summarizeWithFallbackResult` rethrow it, and the outermost compaction safeguard treats it exactly like the pre-existing abort path (cancel compaction, keep history). Only the response latency changes. This follows the same abort-aware-backoff pattern as the recently merged #109604 (telegram startup probe) and #108561 (discord gateway READY retry).

## Changes

- Pass `sleep: (ms) => sleepWithAbort(ms, params.signal)` to `retryAsync` in `summarizeChunks`.
- Add a regression test: `generateSummary` rejects once with a retryable error, the caller aborts 50ms into the ≥500ms backoff; asserts rejection with the abort reason, wall clock under 400ms, and exactly one `generateSummary` call.

## User Impact

Cancelling a session while compaction is retrying a summary now stops promptly instead of lingering through the remaining backoff.

## Evidence

Exact head: `fe96c958ae2800f35bdffae9eab907d21d04addf`.

**Outside-runner behavior proof** — the production `summarizeInStages` from `src/agents/compaction.ts` is driven directly (no test runner, no mocks) via `node --import tsx` against a real `node:http` loopback model endpoint. The endpoint returns HTTP 400, which the OpenAI SDK does not retry internally, so the only backoff in play is compaction's own `retryAsync` (real production schedule: `attempts: 3, minDelayMs: 500`). The abort fires 200ms after the first failure response is sent — deterministically inside the backoff. History preservation is verified by JSON-snapshotting the caller-owned messages array across the rejection.

After fix — abort mid-backoff rejects in 1ms with the abort reason, exactly one model request, history byte-identical:

```text
$ env -C .worktrees/compaction-retry-abort node --import tsx /tmp/compaction-abort-proof.mts; echo "exit=$?"
[proof] loopback model endpoint listening at http://127.0.0.1:46463
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=proof-local api=openai-completions model=proof-model method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:46463/chat/completions timeoutMs=undefined proxy=none policy=custom
[proof-server] model request #1 POST /chat/completions at +281ms
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=proof-local api=openai-completions model=proof-model status=400 elapsedMs=101 contentType=application/json
[proof-server] AbortController.abort() fired at +485ms (inside retry backoff)
[proof] mode=after outcome=rejected(Error: aborted) abortAtMs=485 abortToRejectMs=1 elapsedMs=486 requests=1 historyPreserved=true verdict=PASS
exit=0
```

Before fix (same script with `src/agents/compaction.ts` from `upstream/main`, restored immediately after): the same abort is ignored until the ≥500ms backoff elapses — rejection arrives 328ms after the abort, and with the summarization-path error (`CompactionError: Request was aborted.`) instead of the abortable-sleep rejection.

```text
[proof] loopback model endpoint listening at http://127.0.0.1:39405
[proof-server] model request #1 POST /chat/completions at +256ms
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=proof-local api=openai-completions model=proof-model status=400 elapsedMs=89 contentType=application/json
[proof-server] AbortController.abort() fired at +459ms (inside retry backoff)
[proof] mode=before outcome=rejected(CompactionError: Request was aborted.) abortAtMs=459 abortToRejectMs=328 elapsedMs=787 requests=1 historyPreserved=true verdict=PASS
exit=1 (after-fix expectations unmet: abort-to-reject 328ms vs 1ms)
```

The discriminating evidence is abort-to-rejection latency (1ms vs 328ms) plus error identity (`Error: aborted` from the abortable sleep vs the error surfaced only after riding out the backoff); conversation history is preserved in both modes (`historyPreserved=true`).

Regression test:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/compaction.summarize-fallback.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Same suite against the pre-change implementation (file at `upstream/main`): the new test fails — the abort is ignored, the loop sleeps through the ~500ms backoff and calls `generateSummary` a second time (1130ms, rejects with the summarization error instead of the abort reason).

`oxlint` clean on both changed files; `tsgo` core project reports no errors in compaction files.

## Intentionally out of scope

- No change to retry counts, delay bounds, or the transient-error classification in `shouldRetry`.
- No change to the compaction safeguard's cancel handling; abort already landed there via other paths.

target.title: feat(browser): add secure per-tab copilot panel
target.body:
Related: #93680

## What Problem This Solves

The browser side-panel copilot needs one isolated agent session per tab without letting page content, another tab, or a stale panel acquire a different browser target or receive another session's events. Closing a tab must also end live delivery and run custody without deleting its transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

This rebuild gives the browser copilot a dedicated canonical device-pairing identity with issued-token reuse, Gateway-owned session subscription allowlists with pre-delivery filtering, and typed tab bindings enforced by the browser tool. Chrome receives a capability-bound panel URL through `chrome.sidePanel.setOptions({ tabId, path, enabled })` for each shared tab; there is no global default panel.

The extension service worker owns session creation, panel capability custody, debugger attachment, subscription, abort, and archival. Tab close first revokes delivery/debugger access and aborts any active run, then marks the Gateway session archived. The transcript remains in that archived Gateway session until normal user/admin session deletion; the extension stores no parallel transcript or silent live-session fallback. Failed abort/archive RPCs remain durable recovery work and retry without restoring access.

Based on @2cb2's side-panel implementation in #93680, which established the product direction and served as the implementation basis for this secure rebuild.

## User Impact

Users can open a copilot panel scoped to the current shared tab. Two tabs receive distinct sessions and histories, unshared tabs get a clear denial/share flow, and closing a tab archives its session while preserving the transcript for later inspection.

## Evidence

| Before: unshared-tab denial | After: isolated active panel |
| --- | --- |
| ![Unshared tab denial](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/207bfca3-87f3-4284-b7e8-f12188440794) | ![Isolated per-tab copilot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06218fdf-ce20-4938-a9d4-58813a915661) |

- Full hosted proof on the runtime head: protocol generation parity, dead-code scans, changed-file formatting and guards, project typecheck, core/extension lint, runtime import cycles, production build, and Chromium E2E passed on [Blacksmith Testbox run 29605834706](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29605834706).

target.title: fix(sessions): honor configured entry caps on writes
target.body:
Closes #109191
Related: #108344

AI-assisted implementation; I reviewed the resulting code and validation.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where session-store writes could silently apply the built-in 500-entry cap instead of the operator's configured `session.maintenance.maxEntries`.

It also locks down the current SQLite cron behavior so an active in-flight cron session is not evicted when durable channel entries already exceed the configured cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cap helper now requires its caller to provide the already-resolved maximum. This removes a silent fallback that could never observe runtime configuration, while preserving the existing maintenance owner boundary where file and SQLite write paths resolve the full policy.

Current production callers already provide that resolved value. The added regressions exercise the actual file-write and SQLite-write paths rather than calling the cap helper directly.

## User Impact

Configured session-entry limits are applied consistently during writes. Active cron lifecycle state remains available across consecutive persistence operations even when protected entries fill the cap, avoiding `CronSessionLifecycleClaimError` from maintenance eviction.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/store.pruning.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.integration.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-accessor.conformance.test.ts`

target.title: fix(matrix): honor abortSignal during startup whoami retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`backfillMatrixAuthDeviceIdAfterStartup` in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/config.ts` checks `params.abortSignal` before and after the startup `whoami` call, and the production caller (`monitor/index.ts`) passes a real signal. But the `whoami` request itself retries via `retryMatrixAuthRequest` with an unabortable backoff (250ms→1.5s). An abort landing inside that backoff was only noticed after the sleep elapsed and a second `whoami` request had been issued.

## Why This Change Was Made

`retryMatrixAuthRequest` now accepts an optional `signal` and sleeps via `sleepWithAbort(ms, signal)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` (same abort-aware helper as the merged #109604/#108561/#108408 sibling fixes). The backfill passes its `params.abortSignal` through `fetchMatrixWhoamiIdentity`. When the abort fires mid-backoff, the sleep's rejection propagates through `retryAsync`; a new `try/catch` in the backfill normalizes it to `undefined`, matching the contract of the existing post-`whoami` aborted checks. Non-abort failures still rethrow, and call sites that pass no signal (`resolveMatrixAuth`, password login) see zero behavior change — `sleepWithAbort(ms, undefined)` degenerates to the plain timer.

## Changes

- Thread an optional `signal` through `retryMatrixAuthRequest` and `fetchMatrixWhoamiIdentity`; backoff sleeps use `sleepWithAbort`.
- Pass `params.abortSignal` at the backfill call site; normalize abort rejection to `undefined` (no deviceId) while real network failures still propagate.
- Regression test: first `whoami` fails with a retryable `ECONNRESET`, abort fires inside the first 250ms backoff; asserts prompt `undefined`, exactly one request, and no deviceId persistence.

## User Impact

Stopping a Matrix account during startup no longer waits out the `whoami` retry backoff or issues a doomed second request; shutdown is prompt and no half-backfilled deviceId is persisted.

## Evidence

Exact head: `61bf06d32fffa32b079f9d641ef3203ec4de6c21`.

**Outside-runner behavior proof** — the production `backfillMatrixAuthDeviceIdAfterStartup` is driven directly (no test runner, no mocks) via `node --import tsx` against a real `node:http` loopback homeserver. The homeserver destroys the socket so `whoami` fails with a real transport `TypeError: fetch failed` (matches production `MATRIX_AUTH_REQUEST_RETRY_RE`); state dir is a real temp dir read back from disk afterward. Abort fires at the 200ms mark, inside the first backoff. A no-abort control scenario in the same run proves non-abort errors still rethrow after the full 3-attempt backoff.

After fix — abort during backoff returns `undefined` at the 200ms mark, exactly one `whoami` request, nothing persisted:

target.title: feat: agent_settled extension event for true session idle
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Extensions have no way to know when a session is *truly* idle. `agent_end` fires per run, but automatic continuations follow it: retries, compaction continuations, and queued follow-up deliveries each start another run. An extension that wants "the agent is done — safe to snapshot/notify/hand off" has to guess.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a typed `agent_settled` extension event that fires exactly once when no automatic continuation remains. The post-run handler's boolean loop is refactored into a closed action union (`continue | settled | handoff`), which also makes the recent handoff rule explicit in types: runs that end in a deliberate turn handoff (a yielded parent awaiting external subagent delivery) do **not** settle — external delivery owns the next run.

## User Impact

Plugin authors get a reliable idle signal (`api.on("agent_settled", ...)`). Settlement means idle, not success: failed or aborted non-handoff runs still settle. No behavior change for existing events.

## Evidence

- New regression tests: normal run emits `agent_end` then exactly one `agent_settled`; a queued follow-up produces no intermediate settlement and one final one; handoff-terminated runs emit zero settlement events (13 tests in `agent-session-loop-correctness`).
- **Live verification (real API key):** `node scripts/test-live.mjs -- src/agents/sessions/agent-session.live.test.ts` — 3/3 end-to-end agent runs against a real Claude model on the reshaped post-run path.
- Plugin-SDK API baseline regenerated via the sanctioned workflow; `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` green; full changed-file gate green on hosted runner (run 29612560478); autoreview clean.

Also assessed (no code): explicit `${ENV_VAR}` config references are already covered by the existing SecretRef mechanism (`src/config/types.secrets.ts`, documented in `docs/gateway/secrets.md`) — no new config surface warranted.

target.title: feat(slack): support Agent View
target.body:
Closes #103673

AI-assisted: implemented and reviewed with Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

New Slack AI apps use Agent View, while OpenClaw's generated workspace manifests and DM routing still assumed the older Assistant View lifecycle. Agent View conversations could therefore lose their visible-root session boundary, reply/status threading, and active Slack context; replacing the manifest also risked breaking existing Assistant View installs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generated workspace manifests now use Slack's irreversible `agent_view` migration shape, while runtime support for existing `assistant_view` installs remains intact. Agent-only signals are recorded durably, each visible Agent View root gets its own OpenClaw thread session, replies and status stay on that root, and ordered active-view entities enter the agent only through structured untrusted context. Enterprise Grid remains on its documented V1-only message path and is not migrated by this change.

## User Impact

New Slack apps can use the current Agent View experience without losing conversation isolation or context. Existing Assistant View apps continue working and can choose when to perform Slack's irreversible migration.

## Evidence

- Official contracts checked: Slack's Agent development guide, Agent Messages-tab migration notice, context-management guide, app manifest reference, and `message.im` event reference.
- AWS Crabbox `run_3524e7e5c6a3`: 9 Slack test files, 193 tests passed on Linux/Node 24.

  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format.   • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.1. #4019

All components except the repository name are optional.   • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

target.title: fix(config): render validation array indices with brackets
target.body:
Related: #104854

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading `openclaw config validate` output would see array indexes as dotted object properties, for example `agents.list.0.tools.profile` instead of `agents.list[0].tools.profile`.

This is limited to human-facing validation output. It does not add line numbers or rejected-value rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ConfigValidationIssue.path` is a machine-readable dot path used by JSON, gateway, daemon, and other shared consumers. This revision keeps that contract unchanged and applies bracket notation only while formatting terminal issue lines.

The formatter traverses the include/env-resolved `snapshot.sourceConfig`, so it brackets a numeric segment only when its actual parent is an array. Numeric object keys such as `diagnostics.otel.headers.0` remain dotted. No validation producer, protocol field, or persisted config shape changes.

## User Impact

Human CLI output distinguishes arrays from object properties:

```text
Before: agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting
After:  agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting
```

Machine output remains compatible:

```json
{ "path": "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting" }
```

## Evidence

Current-head live proof used a root config that `$include`d the invalid `agents.list` entry and also contained the numeric object key `diagnostics.otel.headers.0`.

```text
node --import tsx src/entry.ts config validate
OpenClaw config is invalid: <redacted>/openclaw.json
  ? diagnostics.otel.headers.0: Invalid input: expected string, received boolean
  ? agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Invalid input: expected boolean, received string (allowed: true, false)
terminal_exit=1
```

```json
{
  "valid": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "diagnostics.otel.headers.0",
      "message": "Invalid input: expected string, received boolean"
    },
    {
      "path": "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting",
      "message": "Invalid input: expected boolean, received string (allowed: true, false)",
      "allowedValues": ["true", "false"]
    }
  ]
}
```

Focused coverage on head `8f26d7e72c7`:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/issue-format.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` - 2 files passed, 136 tests passed
- repository `oxfmt` on the touched files - passed
- single-file test typecheck - no `src/cli/config-cli.test.ts` errors
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD` - passed
- current-head GitHub CI: 80 passed, 35 scope-skipped, no failed or pending checks

Tests cover invalid issues, valid warnings, `$include`-resolved arrays, binding-union paths, manual issues, numeric object keys, absent display context, and unchanged `--json` paths.

## Possible call chain / impact

```text
config file + $include/env resolution
  -> snapshot.sourceConfig
  -> validation issues keep dotted paths
  -> config validate --json serializes dotted paths unchanged
  -> non-JSON config validate passes sourceConfig as displayRoot
  -> terminal formatter brackets only real array indexes
```

Unaffected surfaces include `ConfigValidationIssue.path`, JSON and gateway responses, daemon/status summaries, config get/set path syntax, validation producers, and numeric record keys.

target.title: refactor(channels): move inbound turn execution into core
target.body:
Related: #109316

Follow-up to #109716.

## What Problem This Solves

Bundled message channels still owned the core execution half of inbound turns: session recording, dispatcher construction, durable-delivery handling, retry plumbing, reply pipelines, and final lifecycle callbacks. That kept deprecated low-level compatibility calls alive as internal architecture even after the marker sweep reached zero removable declarations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core now owns the complete inbound turn lifecycle. Channel adapters return data-only turn plans containing normalized context plus transport delivery facts; the core runner performs recording, dispatch, retry, durable delivery, typing/reaction lifecycle composition, and finalization. Feishu, iMessage, Matrix, Mattermost, Microsoft Teams, QQBot, Signal, Telegram, and WhatsApp now use that path. Special native Mattermost interactions use the focused core reply seam instead of rebuilding lifecycle logic.

Microsoft Teams folds its sender-timezone fact into the effective per-turn config before handing the plan to core. This preserves the existing behavior without keeping the deprecated dispatcher or adding a one-channel field to the public SDK.

The public Plugin SDK declaration baseline is unchanged. A ratcheted guard rejects bundled production use of prepared-turn callbacks, pre-dispatch failure callbacks, and low-level dispatcher lifecycle calls.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. External plugins keep the shipped compatibility window. Maintainers get transport-thinner channels, one core execution path, and a hard zero budget for internal deprecated channel lifecycle calls.

Non-test TypeScript using the task's `*.test.ts` exclusion: **+1797 / -1895, net -98 lines**.

target.title: fix(agents): keep subagent run ID mask from splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the subagent run-ID mask used in lifecycle log/error metadata could emit isolated UTF-16 surrogate halves when the run ID contains astral characters (e.g., emoji).

## Why This Change Was Made

`maskRunId` sliced its prefix/suffix with raw `String.prototype.slice`, which can bisect surrogate pairs. It now uses the repository's existing `sliceUtf16Safe` helper so the masked ID always falls on valid UTF-16 boundaries. The helper lives at module scope; after the hardened deadcode gate flagged the test-only export, coverage now exercises it through the lifecycle controller's public warning surface instead of a direct import.

## User Impact

Subagent lifecycle warnings and error metadata remain well-formed when run IDs contain non-BMP characters.

## Evidence

- Moved `maskRunId` to module scope in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` and exported it.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` covering ASCII masking and astral boundary cases.
- Existing lifecycle controller tests continue to pass.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** Before the patch, a run ID like `"abc😀xxxxxxxxx"` produced `"abc\ud83d…\ude00xxxx"` (isolated surrogate halves). After the patch it returns `"abc…xxxx"`.
- **Real environment tested:** Local checkout of `fix/mask-runid-utf16` at `71f75fbfa526d0041851c3530662325cc35ac424`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; for (const v of ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b", "short"]) console.log(JSON.stringify(maskRunId(v)));'
  ```
  And to verify the masked values survive a real disk round-trip without corrupting:
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e 'import { maskRunId } from "./src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts"; import { writeFileSync, readFileSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs"; import { tmpdir } from "node:os"; import { join } from "node:path"; const f = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "mr-")), "m.txt"); const samples = ["run-1234567890", "abc😀" + "x".repeat(10), "x".repeat(10) + "😀abc", "a😀b"]; const masked = samples.map(maskRunId); writeFileSync(f, masked.join("\n"), "utf8"); const r = readFileSync(f, "utf8"); console.log(r); console.log("round-trip ok:", r === masked.join("\n"));'
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```
  "run-…7890"
  "abc…xxxx"
  "xxxx…abc"
  "***"

  run-…7890
  abc…xxxx
  xxxx…abc
  ***
  round-trip ok: true
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The regression test `does not split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at mask boundaries` passes, `encodeURIComponent` succeeds on every masked value, no isolated surrogates are emitted, and the joined masked values survive a disk write/read round-trip.
- **What was not tested:** No live subagent lifecycle failure path; change is a pure string-formatting helper.

_AI-assisted PR: changes and tests were generated with AI assistance and manually reviewed._



## Follow-up: merge with current main + deadcode policy fix

Merged `upstream/main` (test-file conflict resolved by keeping both the upstream settle-wake block and this mask coverage). Dropped the unnecessary `export` on `maskRunId` to satisfy the hard-zero Knip policy and converted the focused unit test into behavior assertions on `runId` masking in lifecycle finalization warnings (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts` — 106/106 pass). Exact head: `cbc450326c052aade79a5ac929023d962b1aa4e4`.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): treat U+2028/U+2029 as paragraph boundaries when chunking
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Model output can contain Unicode LINE SEPARATOR (U+2028) and PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR (U+2029) characters. `chunkByParagraph()` normalizes `\r\n?` to `\n` for blank-line detection, but does not normalize U+2028/U+2029. When these characters appear instead of `\n\n`, the entire block stays as one fused chunk instead of splitting at paragraph boundaries — producing oversized message chunks on line-oriented channels.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two-step normalization:

1. **U+2029 → `\n\n`** (blank line): U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR is semantically a paragraph boundary, equivalent to a blank line.
2. **U+2028 → `\n`** (single newline): U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR is a single line break within a paragraph.

The two-step order ensures consecutive U+2028  also produces a blank line (`\n` + `\n\n` = `\n\n\n` — blank line detected by `\n[\t ]*\n+`).

## User Impact

Prevents oversized single-chunk messages on line-oriented channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Signal, iMessage, Discord) when model output contains Unicode line/paragraph separators instead of standard `\n\n`.

## Evidence

### Proof: standalone U+2029 splits at paragraph boundary

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { chunkByParagraph } from "./src/auto-reply/chunk.ts";
// Lone U+2029: must split (old code: stayed fused as one chunk)
const r = chunkByParagraph("paragraph one paragraph two starts here", 39);
console.log(JSON.stringify(r));
'
["paragraph one","paragraph two starts here"]
```

**Before fix**: standalone ` ` → `\n` (single LF) → blank-line detector `\n\n+` finds nothing → `["paragraph one\nparagraph two starts here"]` — **fused as one chunk**  
**After fix**: standalone ` ` → `\n\n` (blank line) → detector matches → `["paragraph one", "paragraph two starts here"]` — **splits at paragraph boundary**

### Proof: standalone U+2028 stays as intra-paragraph line break

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { chunkByParagraph } from "./src/auto-reply/chunk.ts";
const r = chunkByParagraph("line one line two same paragraph", 50);
console.log(JSON.stringify(r));
'
["line one\nline two same paragraph"]
```

**U+2028 → `\n` — single newline, no blank line → stays within one paragraph.** Matches standard `\n` behavior.

### Proof: consecutive U+2028  forms blank line

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { chunkByParagraph } from "./src/auto-reply/chunk.ts";
const unicode = chunkByParagraph("paragraph one line  paragraph two starts here", 40);
const newlines = chunkByParagraph("paragraph one line\n\nparagraph two starts here", 40);
console.log(JSON.stringify({unicode, newlines, match: unicode[0] === newlines[0] && unicode[1] === newlines[1]}));
'
{"unicode":["paragraph one line","paragraph two starts here"],"newlines":["paragraph one line","paragraph two starts here"],"match":true}
```

### Observed result

| Input | Behavior | Match \n\n? |
|-------|----------|------------|
| lone U+2029 | → `\n\n` → splits into 2 paragraphs | ✅ |
| lone U+2028 | → `\n` → stays in 1 paragraph | ✅ |
| U+2028  | → `\n\n\n` → splits into 2 paragraphs | ✅ |

### What was not tested

Live model output carrying real Unicode separators on a channel.

## Regression Test Plan

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/chunk.test.ts --run
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  71 passed (71)
```

```
$ npx oxlint src/auto-reply/chunk.ts src/auto-reply/chunk.test.ts — exit 0
```

```
$ git diff upstream/main --stat — 2 files changed, 30 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)
```

Three new tests:
1. Lone U+2029 → paragraph boundary (old test only covered consecutive U+2028 )
2. Lone U+2028 → single line break within paragraph
3. Consecutive U+2028  → combined blank line → identical output to \n\n

Branch rebased on upstream main.

## Root Cause

In `chunkByParagraph()` (`src/auto-reply/chunk.ts:209`), the normalization regex `/ \r\n?|[  ]/g` maps both U+2028 and U+2029 to a single `\n`. But paragraph detection requires a blank-line sequence `\n\n+`. Standalone U+2029 produces only one `\n`, so the blank-line detector never fires — the paragraph remains fused. The original test accidentally masked this because it placed U+2028 and U+2029 consecutively, producing two normalized `\n` characters that formed the required blank line. The fix uses a two-step normalization: U+2029 (= paragraph break) maps to `\n\n` first, then U+2028/U+2028/rn? (= line break) map to `\n`.

target.title: fix(perplexity): send Search API date filters with official field names
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who run Perplexity web search with `date_after` or `date_before` would not get the requested published-date filtering on the native Perplexity Search API path.

OpenClaw exposes `date_after` and `date_before` as user-facing web search parameters. Those values are validated and converted from `YYYY-MM-DD` into Perplexity's expected `M/D/YYYY` date format, but the final native Search API request used the wrong JSON field names:

- `search_after_date`
- `search_before_date`

Perplexity's Search API documents the fields as:

- `search_after_date_filter`
- `search_before_date_filter`

Example before this change:

```json
{
  "query": "OpenClaw releases",
  "date_after": "2024-01-01",
  "date_before": "2024-06-30"
}
```

OpenClaw correctly validated the date range and converted it to Perplexity-style dates, but the outbound request body used non-contract field names:

```json
{
  "query": "OpenClaw releases",
  "max_results": 5,
  "search_after_date": "1/1/2024",
  "search_before_date": "6/30/2024"
}
```

That means users asking for a bounded Perplexity search could receive an API validation error or unbounded results instead of results constrained to the requested publication window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Perplexity native Search API request body now uses the documented date-filter fields while preserving OpenClaw's existing user-facing `date_after` / `date_before` parameter names.

The request body construction is kept local to the Perplexity provider runtime and reused by the existing Search API dispatch path. This keeps the fix scoped to the provider-owned API mapping and does not add configuration, SDK surface, new provider behavior, or any OpenRouter/chat-completions compatibility changes.

The OpenRouter and Perplexity chat-completions path is intentionally unchanged. OpenClaw already rejects Search API-only filters on that path with explicit user-facing errors.

## User Impact

Users can now rely on Perplexity native Search API date filters to constrain results by publication date.

This matters for workflows such as:

- searching only releases or announcements published in a specific window
- excluding stale search results when investigating recent behavior
- comparing search results before and after a product or dependency change
- running date-bounded research prompts through OpenClaw's web search tool

The visible user-facing parameters remain the same:

```json
{
  "date_after": "2024-01-01",
  "date_before": "2024-06-30"
}
```

Only the provider-facing Perplexity request body changes.

## Evidence

Source and contract evidence:

- OpenClaw's Perplexity provider advertises `date_after` and `date_before` for the native Search API path: `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.ts`
- The runtime validates `date_after` / `date_before`, rejects invalid ranges, and converts ISO dates through `isoToPerplexityDate`: `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`
- Before this change, the Perplexity native Search API body used `search_after_date` and `search_before_date`: `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`
- Perplexity's official Search API reference documents `search_after_date_filter` and `search_before_date_filter`: https://docs.perplexity.ai/api-reference/search-post

Focused regression coverage:

- `extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.test.ts` executes the provider tool and inspects the serialized native Search API request body at the guarded-endpoint seam.
- It verifies both official field names and the existing `YYYY-MM-DD` to `M/D/YYYY` conversion without exporting a production-only test helper.

Focused validation:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.test.ts
```

Result:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       17 passed (17)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.29s
```

Live Perplexity proof at head `980f609336c0c88df420eac6317bb2a9769d0aab`:

- Ran the real `createPerplexityWebSearchProvider` tool path with `date_after=2024-01-01` and `date_before=2024-06-30` against `https://api.perplexity.ai/search`.
- The API accepted the request and returned 5 dated results; all 5 dates were inside the requested range.

```json
{"error":null,"provider":"perplexity","count":5,"datedCount":5,"dates":["2024-05-13","2024-05-01","2024-05-09","2024-06-10","2024-05-13"],"allDatedResultsWithinRange":true}
```

Hosted changed gate:

```bash
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.runtime.ts extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.test.ts
```

Result: passed on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxs5y6dst8v3myxhgby7vt9k`, including formatting, Plugin SDK manifest, extension production/test typechecks, lint, boundary guards, and import-cycle checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29620301305

target.title: fix: doctor upgrade 7.2-beta.1 - 7.2-beta.2 fails on fractional restart handoffs
target.body:
Closes #110237

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users upgrading from `2026.7.2-beta.1` could have `openclaw doctor --fix` abort while migrating the shared state database to SQLite STRICT tables after an update restart recorded fractional trace timestamps.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart-trace timestamps are now canonicalized to integer milliseconds at the restart-handoff persistence boundary. During the existing schema-v2-to-v3 migration, doctor prunes expired transient handoffs and converts only known REAL trace cells on live handoffs before the generic STRICT-table rebuild; the SQLite schema version is unchanged.

## User Impact

Affected upgrades can complete without manual SQLite repair. Expired restart handoffs are discarded as transient state, while valid live handoffs are preserved with canonical integer timing values.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the shipped failure with exact `openclaw@2026.7.2-beta.1` and `openclaw@2026.7.2-beta.2` packages before patching: beta.2 doctor failed copying a REAL restart timestamp into the STRICT INTEGER column and rolled back to schema version 2.
- Focused regression coverage: 97 tests passed across `src/infra/restart-handoff.test.ts` and `src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts`.
- Full `pnpm check:changed` passed, including formatting, core/core-test typechecks, focused lint, import-cycle checks, and SQLite/storage guards.
- [Direct AWS Crabbox upgrade proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_95230b089ff0) (`provider=aws`, run `run_95230b089ff0`):
  - beta.1 packaged Gateway reached `/readyz` before and after a traced SIGUSR1 restart;
  - exact beta.2 reproduced the REAL-to-INTEGER STRICT migration failure and atomic rollback;
  - the packed candidate ran doctor with no manual SQL repair, reached `user_version=3` and schema metadata version 3, made `gateway_restart_handoff` STRICT, and pruned the expired transient row;
  - the packaged candidate reached `/readyz` after restart and CLI/Gateway/RPC all reported `2026.7.2`;
  - the owned AWS lease was released after the run.

target.title: fix(update): classify unreadable plugin manifests separately from parse and migration failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Issue #109833: an unreadable (e.g. root-owned, mode-600) plugin `package.json` blocks the entire gateway with a misleading diagnosis. Three defects compound:

1. `readPackagePayloadManifest` lumps `EACCES`/`EPERM`/IO read failures into the same catch as JSON parse errors, reporting `invalid-package-json` / "Could not parse package.json: EACCES…" for a file that was never read.
2. The failure is funneled through the startup-migration headline — "OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready." — although no migration failed.
3. The guidance recommends `openclaw update repair`, which cannot fix file ownership/permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Maintainer-instructed mechanical scope only:

- `src/cli/update-cli/plugin-payload-validation.ts`: permission/IO read failures now classify as a distinct `unreadable-package-json` reason instead of `invalid-package-json`.
- `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts`: plugin-verification blockers get their own accurate headline ("OpenClaw plugin verification failed; refusing to report the gateway ready.") while genuine state-migration failures keep the existing migration wording. Precedence and fail-closed behavior are unchanged (migration warnings → invalid config → plugin convergence, exactly as before).
- `src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.ts`: permission failures now point at the offending path with ownership/permission remediation instead of `openclaw update repair`.

Explicitly out of scope: whether a configured/enabled plugin with an unreadable payload should degrade-and-boot instead of fail-closed. That is a pending product decision (ClawSweeper `needs-product-decision`); current deliberate fail-closed behavior is preserved and deferred to the plugin-surface owner.

## User Impact

Operators hitting an unreadable plugin file during upgrade now see the true cause (permission failure on a named path) with actionable remediation, instead of a false "migration failure" pointing at repair steps that cannot work. No behavior change for whether startup blocks.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Environment: Linux, Node 24, built CLI from this worktree. The real run used PR head `8b1c51f1921` after merging `origin/main` at `9c2d38a596e`. Before publishing this evidence, the branch was refreshed again to current `origin/main` (`781913025b6`) at final PR head `28a64a12325`; the intervening main commits did not touch any of this PR's six files, and the focused tests were rerun on that final head. Two fresh temporary state roots used the same minimal configured plugin, a canonical tracked install record, and `plugins.entries.proof-unreadable-109833.enabled=true`. The plugin `package.json` was made unreadable by the same non-root user that launched OpenClaw. Paths and the local username/group are redacted below.

For the before run, the three changed production files were restored to byte-exact current-main contents (`git diff --exit-code origin/main -- <three production files>` produced no output), then the CLI was built and launched:

```text
$ stat -c '%A %a %U:%G %n' <MAIN_STATE>/staged/proof-unreadable-109833/package.json
---------- 0 <user>:<group> <MAIN_STATE>/staged/proof-unreadable-109833/package.json

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<MAIN_STATE> OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<MAIN_STATE>/openclaw.json \
    node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <PORT> --auth token --bind loopback
[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Plugin "proof-unreadable-109833" failed post-core payload smoke check (invalid-package-json): Could not parse package.json: EACCES: permission denied, open '<MAIN_STATE>/staged/proof-unreadable-109833/package.json' Run `openclaw update repair` to retry plugin repair. Run `openclaw plugins inspect proof-unreadable-109833 --runtime --json` for details.
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" against the mounted state/config, then restart the container.
EXIT=1
```

The branch sources were restored (`git diff --exit-code HEAD -- <three production files>` produced no output), a fresh forced CLI build completed, and the same scenario ran against a second fresh state root:

```text
$ stat -c '%A %a %U:%G %n' <BRANCH_STATE>/staged/proof-unreadable-109833/package.json
---------- 0 <user>:<group> <BRANCH_STATE>/staged/proof-unreadable-109833/package.json

$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<BRANCH_STATE> OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<BRANCH_STATE>/openclaw.json \
    node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <PORT> --auth token --bind loopback
[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw plugin verification failed; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Plugin "proof-unreadable-109833" failed post-core payload smoke check (unreadable-package-json): Could not read package.json at <BRANCH_STATE>/staged/proof-unreadable-109833/package.json: EACCES: permission denied, open '<BRANCH_STATE>/staged/proof-unreadable-109833/package.json' Fix file access for <BRANCH_STATE>/staged/proof-unreadable-109833/package.json so it is readable by the user running OpenClaw. For EACCES or EPERM, correct its ownership or permissions; otherwise resolve the reported filesystem I/O error, then retry. Run `openclaw plugins inspect proof-unreadable-109833 --runtime --json` for details.
Resolve the plugin verification errors above, then restart the container.
EXIT=1
```

Both invocations exited 1 before readiness; a listener check returned `NO_GATEWAY_LISTENER_ON_29187_OR_29188`. This proves the diagnostic changed while fail-closed behavior did not. The temporary fixture, config, state databases, installed payloads, and mode-000 files were removed afterward (`TEMP_PROOF_STATE_REMOVED`).

### Verification

- Refreshed-head focused test command: `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/plugin-payload-validation.test.ts src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.state-migration.test.ts`
- Result on final refreshed head: 3 files / 77 tests passed across 2 Vitest shards in 3.64s.
- `OPENCLAW_FORCE_BUILD=1 pnpm dev ...` completed separately for the byte-exact current-main and restored branch source trees, supplying the built CLIs used for the two runs.
- `git diff --check` and `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check` passed.
- The original code commit passed the mandatory fresh `autoreview --mode uncommitted` with no actionable findings. This feedback pass changed no code; it only merged current main, reran proof, and updated PR evidence.

### Upgrade compatibility and scope

The stored-data-model flag is a false positive from touching startup/doctor and plugin-record consumers: this patch changes only transient discriminated-union values and rendered diagnostics. It does not change config shape, installed-plugin-index serialization, SQLite schema/version, migration inputs/outputs, or persisted state. The same existing state/record shape was accepted by both the current-main and branch runs, so no migration or backfill is required.

Not tested: a live Windows `EPERM` setup or a self-update that mutates the installed OpenClaw package. The real Linux startup run exercises the shared post-core convergence path with an actual `EACCES`; focused tests cover both startup headline separation and update-path outcome coherence. The configured-plugin fatality question is intentionally not changed or tested as a new behavior; it remains deferred to the plugin-surface owner.

Refs #109833.
